PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL - ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
TO: Whitfield deal team (G. Collier, R. Yoon); FROM: Thornburg & Kessler; RE: Verdana - Seller markup (May 2, 2025), negotiation analysis for May 12 session. Preliminary response due to Ashcroft May 8.

1. BOTTOM LINE
The markup is an aggressive retrade: price up $38.4M (9.0x), cash at close up $61.3M, protections cut in almost every category, and three binding-provision attacks (exclusivity, financing, forum). It also appears to be a re-typed baseline, not a true redline: several changes are untracked (section 8). Do not sign or treat it as agreed. Recommend: (a) send a protective letter now on exclusivity and financing; (b) hold the line on environmental, exclusivity, forum and employee guarantee; (c) trade on price structure, basket, premium split, non-compete scope and escrow size within IC authority (8.5x on $38.6M = $328.1M EV, approved April 8). Anything above that, or any financing-out concession, needs IC re-approval (IC memo calls the financing condition "non-negotiable at this stage").

2. THREATS TO BINDING TERMS (address first)
a) Exclusivity. Original s.11 is binding: 60 days to June 13, 2025, no fiduciary out, covers Sellers and the Company. The markup (i) cuts to 45 days (May 29), (ii) adds a fiduciary out with a subjective "Superior Proposal" test, and (iii) adds a 1.5% forward break fee as sole remedy. Sellers cannot amend a binding covenant unilaterally; a change needs mutual written assent. Ms. Ashcroft's email concedes Sellers "entered into the exclusivity arrangement" and says "several parties" have expressed interest. The fee ($5.2M) is a cheap option to breach exclusivity, and sole-remedy language removes injunctive relief. Position: no out; exclusivity runs to the later of June 13 or signing target, auto-extending while negotiating in good faith. Fallback only: out limited to unsolicited, fully financed all-cash bid at least 7.5-10% higher, 10 business days' notice, rolling matching rights, fee at least 3% plus expenses and a 12-month tail. Confirm we hold the fully executed copy (file copy is unsigned; accept the markup's individual Seller signatures, which improve enforceability). Demand written confirmation that no solicitation, discussions or information-sharing has occurred since April 14, and reserve rights (Chancery specific performance/injunction under s.16).
b) Financing letters by May 5. The original has no commitment-letter obligation; the 21-day date is invented and arrives three days after delivery of the markup. The IC memo says no commitment letters exist and expects them mid-to-late May (Crestfield targeted June 30). Making delivery a binding obligation whose failure is a "material breach" (new s.17(f)) would hand Sellers a pretext to exit exclusivity. Reject; do not sign. Reply truthfully (do not overstate; two lenders have indicated willingness to underwrite $155M; no executed letters). Offer: Fund III equity commitment letter plus debt commitment papers at definitive agreement signing, with an interim lender-status call.
c) Forum. Texas law and AAA arbitration (Houston seat, three arbitrators, non-appealable) would also govern the binding provisions. Keep Delaware law/Chancery (Delaware corporation; Delaware choice-of-law statute 6 Del. C. s.2708 supports it). Texas arbitration removes Chancery's quick injunctive remedy for exclusivity.

3. PRICE AND EBITDA
- Seller: 9.0x x $38.6M = $347.4M EV; equity $306.2M (+$38.4M). Effective headline with max $15M earnout: $362.4M EV (9.4x on $38.6M; 9.5x on $38.1M).
- Sellers' counter-argument on s.2(b) is fair: our $309.0M was computed on $38.6M, so we cannot also insist on $38.1M ($304.8M). Recommend conceding $38.6M as a fixed pricing figure, in exchange for Sellers' written withdrawal of the warranty add-back and a no-further-adjustment clause, and using the $0.5M as a chip.
- Warranty reserve $0.7M: reject. A reserve release increases earnings, so normalization is a deduction ($37.9M), not an add-back; the CFO's roll-forward (provision 0.8, claims paid 1.5; reserve 4.0 to 3.3) shows a balance-sheet decline from claims paid, not a P&L credit. Also lock the same definition for the earnout so it cannot be added back for FY2026.
- Arithmetic and quality-of-earnings flags (resolve internally and with Crestfield before May 12; do not volunteer): (1) the four add-backs total $5.6M (2.4+1.8+0.9+0.5), not $5.5M; accepted three total $5.1M, so the "Buyer-preferred" figure is $38.2M, not $38.1M (IC memo and Crestfield repeat the error). Seller could argue $38.7M. (2) CFO workbook "Reported EBITDA" $33.1M equals FY2024 operating income (EBIT); D&A of $6.7M is not added back, and the bridge to it uses a $6.6M "reclassification" plug. Either EBITDA is mislabeled (which would cut in Sellers' favor) or the P&L is; Crestfield should reconcile.
- Recommended price path: open at $309.0M upfront, no earnout (reaffirms 8.0x, closes EBITDA). Target settlement $312-318M upfront (about 8.1-8.2x) plus a capped earnout so that total EV including maximum earnout does not exceed $328.1M. Walk-away without IC: $328.1M all-in.
- Earnout (up to $15M on FY2026 EBITDA over $44.0M, 5.0x slope, full payout at $47.0M) is a concession we can use, but not as drafted. Seller's own trend (8.6% revenue growth, 20.6% adjusted margin) yields about $45.5M in FY2026 with no help from us, i.e., about $7.5M payable for status quo performance, and our planned cost savings ($4.5-5.0M) would push toward full payout, so we would pay twice for our own synergies. Counter: threshold about $46.5M, cap $10-12M, fixed accounting definitions excluding Buyer-initiated savings, acquisitions and new add-backs; delete the absolute operating covenants (capex, expense timing, past practice) that conflict with the 100-day plan, keeping a narrow primary-purpose covenant; indemnity set-off.

4. CONSIDERATION, ESCROW, FINANCING MATH
Sellers' mix (90% cash/5% rollover/5% escrow) raises closing cash from $214.2M to $275.6M and cuts rollover from $26.8M to $15.3M (about 9.6% of Lanford's 52% proceeds): less alignment for a founder-dependent business. Indicative cash uses at Sellers' structure: $275.6M + $15.3M escrow funding + $46.2M debt payoff + $8-10M costs = about $345-347M, versus planned sources of about $310M ($155M debt at 4.0x, $155M equity): a shortfall of roughly $30-36M (about 4.9x leverage or a 20%+ larger equity check), plus the 112.5% of salary retention payable at close. Positions: 80-85% cash, 8-10% rollover (Lanford-led, Buyer election, same economic terms as our equity, restored from original), balance escrow.
Escrow: concede general indemnity escrow to about 5% with 15 months (no 6-month interim release, or 25% at 9 months only if no claims), but add a separate environmental escrow tied to EPA audit and long-tail survival. R&W insurance does not justify Seller's cuts: it excludes known matters (Baton Rouge fine, Houston audit) and often pollution; ask Pinnacle for draft exclusions before May 12.

5. INDEMNITY AND REPS
- Environmental special indemnity (highest priority; Crestfield, IC): Seller's $10M cap/48 months is about 3% of EV versus Crestfield's 25% of EV (about $77M)/6 years floor. Hold uncapped, survival through statute of limitations or at least 6-7 years; only fallback: cap at least 25% of EV with 6-year survival. Note Seller silently removed the named items (DEQ fine, EPA Tier 2 audit) from the indemnity text.
- Cap 15% to 10%: concede to 12.5% only with fundamental reps, taxes, fraud, covenants outside cap (original carve-out at Equity Value was silently dropped). Basket: Seller's 1.5% tipping basket ($4.59M) is better for Buyer than our true deductible once losses exceed $4.59M; accept tipping, negotiate to 1.0% and De minimis $75K to $100K max.
- Reps: restore undisclosed liabilities, sufficiency of assets, customer/supplier (47% concentration), plus no-conflicts and related-party reps silently dropped (Lanford-Cho). R&W coverage exists only for reps in the agreement, as Seller's own comment concedes. Accept knowledge qualifiers only for non-environmental, non-fundamental reps, add Briggs and EHS lead to knowledge group, constructive knowledge, materiality scrape. Survival: 18 months general (12 would expire before the first post-closing audit cycle is stale), fundamental 36 months (concede 30 if needed). R&W premium: concede 50/50 as a low-cost trade, but expenses paragraph also shifts Redwood's fees to the Company (i.e., Buyer): treat as Seller transaction expense reducing price.
- Exclusive remedy: markup narrowed carve-outs to "fraud" only, dropping willful breach and equitable relief (needed to enforce non-competes). Restore.

6. CLOSING CONDITIONS
- MAE: Seller deleted the "disproportionate effect" qualifiers on general-economy and industry carve-outs, dropped "operations" and "liabilities," and added pandemics, announcement/pendency and projection-miss carve-outs. Restore disproportionality; accept announcement carve-out only excluding reps on consents/conflicts; reject projection carve-out or keep Seller's own parenthetical.
- Bring-down: "in all respects except MAE" is the most Seller-friendly formulation. Counter: fundamental reps true in all respects (de minimis exceptions), others in all material respects.
- Customer consents: with 47% top-five concentration, convert to a condition limited to identified key customers (top five), or a no-termination/no-notice-of-nonrenewal condition for them. Hargrove consent is unnecessary if debt is repaid (payoff letter; prepayment permitted without penalty); landlord consents/estoppels stay (Wilmington lease ends 12/31/2026).
- Financing: see 2(b). Package: drop the financing condition at signing only if debt commitments and Fund III equity commitment letter are delivered, with reverse break fee as Sellers' sole and exclusive remedy and no specific performance of financing. Seller's 3.0% ($10.4M; arithmetic correct) is acceptable market and the sole-remedy cap is valuable, but it must not apply if any Buyer condition (ESOT approval, HSR, MAE, rep accuracy, consents) fails.
- ESOT: accept "adequate consideration" (ERISA s.3(18), 29 U.S.C. s.1002(18); s.408(e) exemption; not independently verified in this run) plus financial fairness opinion, and a 45-day period only if it runs from delivery of near-final definitive agreement terms, not from the term sheet; an approval deadline at least 15 business days before closing (Crestfield).
- Silently dropped conditions: ancillary deliverables (non-competes, Lanford employment agreement, retention agreements), diligence completion, and the post-closing net debt true-up (60 days). Restore.

7. MANAGEMENT, EMPLOYEES, RESTRICTIVE COVENANTS
- Lanford: markup halves term to 12 months, raises salary to $550K (+15.8%), doubles equity to 4% with undefined vesting, adds Good Reason (including reporting changes) with full single-trigger acceleration. This pays more for less service in a founder-dependent business (Crestfield: minimum 24 months). Counter: 24 months (18 floor), $475-500K, 2-2.5% with performance and time vesting (4-year, original), acceleration only double-trigger on termination without cause/Good Reason after cure period, 6-12 month transition advisory tail.
- Retention 150% base, 75% at close: front-loading defeats retention.
- Employee guarantee (412 employees, 12 months, no terminations without cause, no headcount reduction, no relocation) directly conflicts with the 100-day plan (about 45 positions at Baton Rouge/Wilmington, $4.5-5.0M savings; Wilmington consolidation) and would also undercut the earnout economics. Reject; offer 12-month comparable base pay/benefits for continuing employees, severance at current policy, no third-party beneficiary rights. Do not disclose the internal plan, and do not make any statement denying it (Delaware fraud carve-out risk).
- Non-compete: concede Lanford to 4 years (from 5) nationwide or in all states where the Company sold in the prior 3 years, not "active contracts at Closing" (Seller-controlled, shrinks scope); Lanford-Cho 2.5-3 years; accept 5% passive public holding (no board role).

8. SILENT CHANGES TO CHALLENGE
Seller's "deleted" text does not match our April 14 sheet in many places (financing condition, RBF trigger, bring-down, escrow wording, governing law, section numbering). Untracked differences found: joint and several liability, pre-closing tax indemnity, fundamental/fraud cap carve-out, willful-breach/equitable-relief carve-outs, named environmental matters, two reps, ancillary and diligence conditions, net debt true-up, rollover mechanics, Company as exclusivity party, "Alternative Transaction" definition, expenses added to the binding list, and diligence access limited until antitrust clearance.

9. SESSION PLAN
Before May 8: protective letter (exclusivity in force, no financing obligation exists, compliance confirmation, financing status). Opening package: hold price at 8.0x/$38.6M with warranty add-back withdrawn; trade list in order: R&W premium split, tipping basket, narrower non-competes, general escrow size, earnout (capped, restructured), knowledge qualifiers for non-core reps, 45-day ESOT period, 3% RBF with sole-remedy. Non-negotiables: uncapped (or 25% EV/6-year) environmental indemnity, no fiduciary out, Delaware forum, no employee guarantee, key customer protection, MAE disproportionality, restored carve-outs.
Limits: no research verification of case law/statutes was possible (law.cornell.edu fetch blocked); authorities cited from knowledge and flagged. Document set lacks the executed term sheet and NDA.
